item.title: B.C. to bring in safety zones, ban harassment around sites of worship
item.description: VICTORIA — The British Columbia government is bringing in legislation to prevent intimidation, mental and physical harassment, and obstruction of people from going to their temples, churches and other places of worship. item.title: PRRD offers $250,000 towards new Foundry in Fort St. John
item.description: The Peace River Regional District (PRRD) has tentatively agreed to offer Foundry Fort St. John $250,000 in funding.

item.title: Huskies drop both games to start NWJHL 2025-26 finals
item.description: Seen as underdogs, the Fort St. John Huskies dropped the first two games of the NWJHL finals to the La Crete Lumber Barons on March 7th and 8th.

item.title: Marc Miller says Musqueam deal has ‘nothing to do with’ private property
item.description: OTTAWA — Culture Minister Marc Miller says a rights acknowledgment agreement between the federal government and the Musqueam First Nation has “nothing to do with” private property. item.title: Moose FM radiothon raises $15,000 for Skye’s Place
item.description: Moose FM raised $15,000 at March 6th's radiothon invite. The funds from the event will be donated to the Fort St. John Women's Resource Society's Skye's Place.

item.title: Teams dressed as nuns, wrestlers, film villains and more take to dodgeball court for annual Fort St. John fundraiser
item.description: The dodgeball tournament, organized by the City of Fort St. John's recreational department and the North Peace Gymnastics Association, took place on Saturday, March 7th.

item.title: Fort St. John city salt truck driver involved in crash and issued ticket after allegedly running red light
item.description: A City of Fort St. John salt truck was involved in a crash after allegedly running a red light at the intersection of 100th Street and 100th Avenue on March 8th.

item.title: Tse’k’wa cave wins B.C. tourism award for Indigenous experience
item.description: Charlie Lake's Tse'k'wa Heritage Society won the Indigenous operator or experience award at the Tourism Industry Association of BC (TIABC) conference in Kelowna.

item.title: School District 60 amends annual budget over fewer enrolments
item.description: School District 60 has released the details of its amended budget, showing a drop in enrolments for the school year 2025-26.

item.title: Family sues OpenAI over mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge
item.description: The family of Maya Gebala is suing Open AI after the Tumbler Ridge Shooting.
